{{Short description|Mathematical tool associated with lifting problems}}
{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''deformation ring''' is a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] that controls liftings of a [[group representation|representation]] of a [[profinite group]] (usually a [[Galois group]]) from a [[finite field]] to a [[local ring]]. In particular, for any such lifting problem there is often a '''universal deformation ring''' that classifies all such liftings, and whose [[spectrum of a ring|spectrum]] is the '''universal deformation space'''.

A key step in [[Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem|Wiles's proof]] of the [[modularity theorem]] was to study the relation between universal deformation rings and [[Hecke algebra]]s.

== Coefficient rings and the deformation functor ==
For a (fixed) finite field <math>k</math>, a '''coefficient ring''' for <math>k</math> is a commutative [[Noetherian ring|Noetherian]] [[Local ring|local]] ring <math>(R, \mathfrak{m})</math> which is complete in the <math>\mathfrak{m}</math>-[[adic topology]], whose residue field is identified with <math>k</math>. Write <math>\pi_R : R \twoheadrightarrow k</math> for the quotient map. A '''morphism of coefficient rings''' <math>\varphi : R \to R'</math> is a continuous homomorphism of local rings such that <math>\pi_R = \pi_{R'} \circ \varphi</math>. The [[Category theory|category]] of coefficient rings will be denoted <math>\mathcal{C}</math>.

For example, if <math>k = \mathbb{F}_p</math> is the finite field with <math>p</math> elements, then the ring of [[P-adic number#p-adic integers|<math>p</math>-adic integers]] <math>\mathbb{Z}_p</math> as well as its associated [[formal power series ring]] <math>\mathbb{Z}_p[\![X]\!]</math> are both coefficient rings for <math>k</math>, and the inclusion map <math>\mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathbb{Z}_p[\![X]\!]</math> is a morphism of coefficient rings.

The <math>\pi_R</math> maps induce maps <math>(\pi_{R})_* : \mathrm{GL}_n(R) \to \mathrm{GL}_n(k)</math>, whose kernel is denoted <math>\Gamma_n(R)</math>. Thus, any [[group representation]] <math>\rho : G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(R)</math> gives us a related <math>k</math>-valued representation <math>\overline{\rho} : G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(k)</math> via <math>\overline{\rho} := \pi_R \circ \rho</math>. Such <math>\overline\rho</math> is called the '''residual representation''' of <math>\rho</math>.

Two continuous representations <math>\rho_1,\rho_2 : \Pi \to \mathrm{GL}_n(R)</math> of a profinite group <math>\Pi</math> are said to be '''strictly equivalent''' if there exists <math>M \in \Gamma_n(R)</math> such that <math display="inline">M^{-1}\rho_1 M = \rho_2.</math> This is stronger than the usual [[Group representation#Definitions|isomorphism of representations]], since we require that the isomorphism <math>\rho_1 \stackrel{\sim}{\rightarrow} \rho_2</math> induces the identity map on residual representations.

A '''deformation''' of <math>\overline{\rho} : \Pi \to \mathrm{GL}_n(k)</math> to a coefficient ring <math>R</math> is a strict equivalence class of continuous lifts of <math>\overline\rho</math> through the reduction map <math>(\pi_R)_* : \mathrm{GL}_n(R) \to \mathrm{GL}_n(k)</math>. Informally, any continuous lift <math>\rho : \Pi \to \mathrm{GL}_n(R)</math> may be referred to as a deformation of <math>\overline\rho</math>, but in this sense two deformations are considered the same if and only if the underlying representations are strictly equivalent. Let <math>\mathrm{Def}_{\overline\rho}(R)</math> denote the set of deformations of <math>\overline\rho</math> to <math>R</math>.

Any morphism of coefficient rings <math>\varphi : R \to R'</math> must send <math>\Gamma_n(R)</math> to <math>\varphi_*[\Gamma_n(R)] \subseteq \Gamma_n(R')</math>, so if we fix a residual deformation <math>\overline\rho</math>, we see that composition with <math>\varphi_*</math>sends <math>R</math>-valued deformations of <math>\overline{\rho}</math> to <math>R'</math>-valued deformations of <math>\overline\rho</math>. In other words, <math>\mathrm{Def}_{\overline\rho}</math> defines a (covariant) [[functor]] <math>\mathrm{Def}_{\overline\rho} : \mathcal{C} \to \mathbf{Set}</math>.

== Deformation rings ==
If we fix a residual representation <math>\overline\rho : \Pi \to \mathrm{GL}_n(k)</math>, then under certain conditions (most notably that the representation <math>\overline\rho</math> admits only scalar automorphisms) one can show<ref>{{Citation |last=Mazur |first=B. |chapter=Deforming Galois Representations |date=1989 |title=Galois Groups over ℚ |volume=16 |pages=385–437 |editor-last=Ihara |editor-first=Y. |chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4613-9649-9_7 |access-date=2026-07-29 |place=New York, NY |publisher=Springer US |doi=10.1007/978-1-4613-9649-9_7 |isbn=978-1-4613-9651-2 |editor2-last=Ribet |editor2-first=K. |editor3-last=Serre |editor3-first=J.-P.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ramakrishna |first=Ravi |date=1993 |title=On a variation of Mazur's deformation functor |url=https://www.numdam.org/item/?id=CM_1993__87_3_269_0 |journal=Compositio Mathematica |language=en |volume=87 |issue=3 |pages=269–286 |issn=1570-5846}}</ref> that the deformation functor <math>\mathrm{Def}_{\overline\rho}</math> is [[Representable functor|representable]]'','' in that there exists some coefficient ring <math>R_{\overline\rho}</math> such that <math>\mathrm{Def}_{\rho}(R') \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(R_{\overline\rho}, R')</math>. Such a coefficient ring <math>R_{\overline\rho}</math> is called a '''(universal) deformation ring''' for <math>\overline\rho</math>. Consequently, any deformation <math>\rho : \Pi \to \mathrm{GL}_n(R_{\overline\rho})</math> of <math>\overline\rho</math> must be of the form <math>\rho = \varphi_* \circ \rho_{\mathrm{univ}}</math> for some deformation <math>\rho_{\mathrm{univ}} : \Pi \to \mathrm{GL}_n(R_{\overline\rho})</math> and some <math>\varphi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathcal{C}}(R_{\overline\rho})</math>. The pair <math>(R_{\overline\rho}, \rho_{\mathrm{univ}})</math> is called a '''universal deformation''' of <math>\overline\rho</math>.

More concisely, such a pair <math>(R_{\overline\rho}, \rho_{\mathrm{univ}})</math> is uniquely characterised by the following [[universal property]]: if <math>R</math> is any coefficient ring and <math>\rho : \Pi \to \mathrm{GL}_n(R)</math> is any deformation of <math>\overline\rho</math> to <math>R</math>, then there is a unique <math>\mathcal{C}</math>-morphism <math>\varphi : R_{\overline\rho} \to R</math> such that <math>\rho = \varphi_* \circ \rho_{\mathrm{univ}}</math>. As a consequence of this universal property, deformation rings are unique up to unique isomorphism.

== Example in dimension 1 ==
For <math>p</math> an odd prime number and <math>\Pi = G_{\Q, S}</math> the [[absolute Galois group]] of the rational numbers with ramification restricted to <math>S = T \cup \{p\}</math>, where <math>T</math> is the set of primes dividing <math>p-1</math>. Let <math>\varepsilon : \Pi \to \mathbb{F}_p^\times
</math> denote the <math>p</math>-adic cyclotomic character given by<math display="block">\Pi \twoheadrightarrow \mathrm{Gal}(\Q(\zeta_p)/\Q) \,\stackrel{\sim}{\to}\, \mathbb{F}_p^\times,</math>with <math>\zeta_p = e^{2 \pi i /p}</math> a primitive <math>p</math>th [[root of unity]]. One can show in this case that deformation ring is exactly the completed [[group ring]] <math>\Z_p[\![\Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}}]\!]</math>, where <math>\Gamma</math> is the maximal pro-<math>p</math>-quotient of <math>\Pi</math>, and a universal deformation for <math>\varepsilon</math> is given by <math display="block">\chi_{\mathrm{univ}} : G_{\Q} \to \Z_p[\![\Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}}]\!]^\times;\qquad \sigma \mapsto \hat{\varepsilon}(\sigma)\varpi(\sigma),</math>where <math>\hat{\varepsilon} : \Pi \to \Z_p^\times</math> is the composition of <math>\varepsilon</math> with the [[Teichmüller character]], and <math>\varpi : \Pi \twoheadrightarrow \Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}}</math> is the quotient map.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.ams.org/pcms/009 |title=Arithmetic Algebraic Geometry |date=2008-02-07 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=978-0-8218-4448-9 |editor-last=Conrad |editor-first=Brian |series=IAS/Park City Mathematics Series |volume=9 |location=Providence, Rhode Island |language=en |doi=10.1090/pcms/009/05 |editor-last2=Rubin |editor-first2=Karl}}</ref>
